sources.observation: DICTIONARYVAR uses group 330 to identify its ACDBVARIABLEDICTIONARY owner; its schema and value are separate payload fields.

The named-object dictionary example lists AcDbVariableDictionary as an NOD child and lists variable names beneath it. The documentation also states that dictionaries are containers and dictionary entries carry hard ownership references.

planImpact.implementationSummary: Corrected the shared named-resource and focused DICTIONARYVAR generated ASCII/Binary controls from direct-NOD typed leaves to NOD[AcDbVariableDictionary] -> child DICTIONARY -> DICTIONARYVAR leaves. Readback checks follow the dictionary entry and owner path through raw replay and synthetic typed serialization. Strict writer graph preflight now rejects direct-NOD, duplicate-key, wrong-kind, missing-target, and wrong-owner routes before destination replacement. Positive controls cover mixed group-350/group-360 input, subordinate objects preceding their referenced child dictionary while retaining the required first-record NOD, regenerated-NOD group-350 output, and ordinary child dictionary hard-owner-dependent output. The plan reconciles current local status against the older 2025 readiness snapshot.

method.generatedScratchControls: Existing ASCII and Binary DXF test controls regenerated at runtime; no drawing fixture file added.
method.limitations: This proves local strict-writer graph admission and generated ASCII/Binary DXF roundtrip behavior for the documented dictionary topology plus a compatibility-only group-360 input. It is not a real DWG parser witness, independent producer result, or native-consumer result. Autodesk documents group 350; the group-360 test is compatibility evidence only.
